item.title: SHARK WEEK Hoo Ha Ha — Fri Jul 31, 12:00 PM — DSSOLVR
item.description:
All week – shark week screenings, themed cocktails, photobooth, carnival game, snack bags, & more! Come to the shark side & celebrate Shark Week at DSSOLVR! All day all week: Sunday, July 26th – Saturday, August 1st – Shark week on the TVs all week! (play some free shark week bingo cards or color some shark themed coloring pages while you watch – adults like to color too :) – Jaw-some themed cocktails & jello-shots – Fin-omenal photobooth (become the shark) – Goth the Munchies? We will have Shark Snack Bags! (a variety box of ocean themed sweets available all week until sold out) – Sink or Swim Carnival Game – Pick one of the rubber sharks from the mini pool on the bar and see if you win a prize! (One free play per person per day – must be over 21 yrs old to play & win! – some prizes may contain alcohol wink)
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Tour: A Closer Look at "Continental Shift" — Fri Jul 31, 1:00 PM — Ackland Art Museum
item.description:
Join Ackland educators for a lively half-hour look at a small handful of artworks in Continental Shift: Recent Acquisitions of African Art. These engaging conversational tours offer a closer look at and new perspectives on works on view at the Museum. Free, but space is limited to 20 participants; first come, first served. This event is part of UNC–Chapel Hill’s Campus Life Experience (CLE) program. Students who attend can scan the QR code provided at the event to receive CLE credit.
Source: UNC Chapel Hill

item.title: World Ranger Day — Fri Jul 31, 3:00 PM — Stone Mountain State Park
item.description:
Join a Ranger at the Park Visitor Center to celebrate World Ranger Day! Come and learn about what Park Rangers do along with what essentials are kept in our trucks.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Storywalk: Discovering Trees — Sat Aug 1, 9:00 AM — Pilot Mountain State Park
item.description:
August 1st through 31th. Take a walk and read “Discovering Trees” by Backpack Expolrer. Begin at the visitor center and walk the Fiddlehead and Grassy Ridge Trail loop. Follow the pages along the trail. The StoryWalk® Project was created by Anne Ferguson and developed in collaboration with the Kellogg-Hubbard Library in Montpelier Vermont. Storywalk® is a registered service mark owned by the Kellogg-Hubbard Library
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: How Spiritual Humans Become Fully Free in the Multiverse — Sun Aug 2, 11:00 AM
item.description:
Raleigh & Triangle Activities Meetup Group No joke, the multiverse is real and you \*will\* learn to navigate it to set yourself fully free. Free from your post-traumatic stress, free from fascist domination and ecological disaster, free to live happy ever after in the like-minded communities where you belong to thrive. The only question is, how will you learn how the multiverse really works? Dramatic misconceptions are common to keep you struggling in domination fantasies of the negative ego. The living loving Universe is actually an elegantly generous and easy creation partner, aka God, Goddess, Great Spirit, Source, etc. Your challenge is to get through the Earth school of mastering false negative belief systems so you can always enjoy recalling who you really are – your own form of the Universe itself, able to remember and revisit your own paradise with increasing clarity.
Join us this Sunday August 2, 2026 for a free empowering talk on the multiverse as the original spiritual tec

item.title: America 250: Colonial Games — Sun Aug 2, 2:00 PM — Weymouth Woods Sandhills Nature Preserve
item.description:
Step back in time and discover the fun of colonial games that children and families enjoyed during early American history! We will have interactive games for you to learn and play!
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Owl Appreciation Day — Tue Aug 4, 10:00 AM — Pilot Mountain State Park
item.description:
Come out to celebrate Owl appreciation day on the mountain! Park staff will have a hands-on owl education table set-up on the mountain, and we will be sharing information on what owls live in the area, how to find them, and what makes them so amazing! Want to see if you're as strong as a great horned owl? Learn the perfect barred owl call? Feel real feathers? Pop over for a hootin' good time! This event is weather permitting sadly and in the event of rain it will be canceled.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: First Tuesday Social Ride — Tue Aug 4, 6:00 PM — CCB Plaza
item.description:
Pull up and ride with us! Black Spoke Society’s First Tuesday rides are no-drop, social-paced group rides built for connection, joy, and getting outside together. Whether you’re brand new to cycling, dusting off your bike, or ride every week, you belong here. We roll at a conversational pace, pause when needed, and make sure no one gets left behind. This is about community over competition. Come as you are. Bring a friend. Bring your whole self. Expect: – A chill, steady pace – Good music and even better vibes – Route support and ride leaders – Water + snack stops when needed – Post-ride hangs when the mood is right Helmet required. Lights encouraged. Good energy mandatory. Let’s ride. 🖤🚴🏾‍♀️
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Morning Canoe Paddle — Wed Aug 5, 10:30 AM — Hanging Rock State Park
item.description:
Join Ranger Carson and start your morning with a peaceful paddle on the park’s lake as we slow down and reconnect with nature. Before we get started, we’ll explore the basics of canoeing and make sure everyone is comfortable on the water. Be sure to bring swimming attire, towel, water, water appropriate shoes, and sunscreen. This is an interactive program with limited space. To register, email carson.orton@ncparks.gov
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: On-Site Fitness Consultations — Wed Aug 5, 12:00 PM — None
item.description:
Health Assessment is a free, confidential health screening provided through Duke benefits. It includes total cholesterol, blood pressure, blood glucose, BMI, waist circumference height, weight and body mass index measurements. Additionally, there is a goal setting and referral session with a nurse, dietitian, or fitness specialist. Many participants find the coaching session helps them get started making lifestyle changes and connects them to LIVE FOR LIFE and community resources to support them. Health Assessments are available to all active Duke employees.
Source: Duke University

item.title: Ask A Ranger — Fri Aug 7, 11:00 AM — Stone Mountain State Park
item.description:
Come ask a Ranger about their dream job and learn more about Stone Mountain State Park.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Junior Ranger Hike — Fri Aug 7, 1:00 PM — Hanging Rock State Park
item.description:
Join a Park Ranger and explore some topics about what makes Hanging Rock State Park special. Learn about what a Park Ranger does, look for creatures, and earn a Junior Ranger badge, all while hiking around our lake. The trail is an easy 1-mile loop. This program is for children ages 5-12 and their families, but all are welcome. Be sure to bring water, good shoes for hiking, and weather appropriate clothing. Registration is required – please email Jackson.perry@ncparks.gov.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Ancient Inspirations — Sat Aug 8, 1:00 PM — North Carolina State Capitol
item.description:
Join the North Carolina State Capitol this August to revisit a special tour series, Ancient Inspirations. Offered every Saturday of the month, learn how the ideas of the ancient Greeks and Romans shaped modern North Carolina and America. Tour topics will include ancient symbolism in art and architecture, citizenship and voting, military service, government, science and mathematics, and many other topics connecting our distant past with the modern day.
Tours will begin at 1 p.m. on August 8, 15, 22, and 29. Tours start outdoors but take place primarily inside the Capitol building. The tours are free, and no reservation is necessary. Walk-ups are encouraged. Tour content is appropriate for most age groups but recommended for ages 10 and up. Tours begin in the Capitol rotunda, please check in at front desk when you arrive.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Smokey Bear — Sun Aug 9, 2:00 PM — Stone Mountain State Park
item.description:
Join a Ranger at the Visitor Center to celebrate Smokey Bear on his birthday by learning his story! There'll be cake!
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Nature Stories at NCMA — Mon Aug 10, 10:30 AM — North Carolina Museum of Art
item.description:
*This program takes place at the North Carolina Museum of Art. Please meet us near the Welcome Center.* Open your eyes to the wonderful world of nature through a family-friendly, nature-filled story time. We’ll begin by sharing a story and will then explore natural themes through hands-on, interactive activities. We may head to other areas of the Art Museum’s campus. This is a free program. Come dressed for the weather and prepared to take a walk. Most walks will be stroller-friendly. Designed for ages 7 & younger – everyone welcome!
Source: NC Museum of Natural Sciences

item.title: Live Animal Feeding – Ocean Habitat — Mon Aug 10, 10:45 AM — Downtown Raleigh
item.description:
Join us for a live feeding of the marine life in the Our Changing Oceans aquarium and meet our Living Collections staff. Species currently in our 10,000-gallon aquarium include:
Angelfish (gray, French) Tangs (Atlantic blue, ocean surgeon, doctorfish) Grunts (bluestriped, French, porkfish) Balloonfish Lobsters
This walk-up program is offered:
Monday, Wednesday & Friday — 10:45am
Location: Nature Research Center, 1st floor, Our Changing Oceans exhibit. No registration required.
Source: NC Museum of Natural Sciences

item.title: Snorkel Quest: HARO Lake — Mon Aug 10, 1:00 PM — Lake Bathhouse
item.description:
Join Ranger Fields and uncover the secret life of Hanging Rock Lake. We will snorkel the swim area, looking for fish, amphibians, and macroinvertebrates. Attendees will need to bring their own snorkel; however, masks/goggles will be available to use. Life jackets will be available along with nets and collecting containers. To sign up for this program, email Jacob.fields@ncparks.gov.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Pilot Knob Hike — Tue Aug 11, 10:00 AM — Pilot Mountain State Park
item.description:
Join a Ranger for a walk around the Big Pinnacle on the Pilot Knob Trail. The trail is 0.8 miles in length, and during the hike we will discuss the history and ecology of the park
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Tot Tuesday: Jr. Ranger Training — Tue Aug 11, 11:00 AM — Pilot Mountain State Park
item.description:
This month for our youngest adventurers we are offering a special opportunity to become real Jr. Rangers with, crafts, soil painting, animal and plant investigation activities, games, and even an interview with a Ranger! Kids receive a signed certificate and prize. This program is rain or shine. For this program please RSVP for updates!
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Snorkel Quest: Up The Dan — Tue Aug 11, 1:00 PM — Dan River Access
item.description:
Join Ranger Fields and snorkel the waters of the Dan River! This is a unique way to beat the heat and observe a cool, natural world. Please bring your own snorkeling mask, however some goggles and masks will be on hand. We’ll plan to snorkel up the Dan River. Note: weather conditions may affect this program days in advance. The location of this program will take place at the Dan River Access. To sign up for this program, email Jacob.fields@ncparks.gov.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: AI Unfiltered: Coffee and Conversation — Wed Aug 12, 9:00 AM — Innovate Carolina Junction
item.description:
Interested in the ever-evolving world of AI?
Join us for AI Unfiltered, a monthly gathering where students, faculty, staff, and community members come together over coffee to explore the fast-moving world of artificial intelligence. Whether you're deeply involved in AI or simply curious about the latest ideas, this is a welcoming space to share insights, ask questions, network, and connect through conversation about all things AI.
Register here! Event is free and open to all.
Source: UNC Chapel Hill

item.title: Story Time at the Museum — Wed Aug 12, 10:30 AM — Downtown Raleigh
item.description:
This is a free program in the Windows on the World classroom, located on the 3rd floor of the Nature Exploration Center in downtown Raleigh. Story Time is designed especially for children 5 and younger and books are chosen with this age group in mind. Join us in the summer on Wednesdays at 10:30am and on Fridays at 10:30am & 11:30am. Please note that we do not guarantee the opportunity to touch live animals during this program. For more information, contact Emma Feichter at emma.feichter@naturalsciences.org or 919.707.9956.
Source: NC Museum of Natural Sciences

item.title: Fishing With a Ranger — Fri Aug 14, 4:30 PM — Morse Park
item.description:

Please note that we are limited to loaner 20 poles. Feel free to bring your own tackle and poles as long as it is in good working order.
Meet at Morse Park in Lake Lure. Parking available at the Lake Lure Marina and public parking in Lake Lure. Admission to the Chimney Rock State Park is not required for this event.

item.title: Black N STEM Conference — Sat Aug 15, 9:00 AM — The Sonja Haynes Stone Center for Research in Black Culture and History
item.description:
Calling All Future Scientists, Engineers & Innovators!
The CommUniversity Youth Program at the Sonja Haynes Stone Center invites K-8th Grade students to an exciting day of exploration, discovery, and inspiration at the Black N STEM Conference!
📅 Saturday, August 15, 2026 (NEW DATE) ⏰ 9 AM – 2 PM 📍 Sonja Haynes Stone Center, UNC-Chapel Hill
Highlights: - Fireside Chat with Tiffany Greene, Sr. Project Manager for Constellation Clean Energy, moderated by Dr. Cheryl Woods Giscombe - Breakfast, lunch, and snacks provided - Transportation included - FREE for all K–8th grade students
This is a wonderful opportunity for young scholars to explore STEM careers, connect with professionals, and see themselves represented in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics.
📲 Register today: go.unc.edu/BlackNSTEM

item.description:
Join a Park Ranger for a morning canoe paddle on our 12-acre lake. Learn the basics of canoeing, why boating safety is important, and what makes our lake special. While there is no swimming portion during this program, you will likely get splashed, so be sure to wear appropriate clothing. Bring water and sunscreen. This program is for everyone, however, anyone 15 years old and younger must be accompanied by an adult. Registration is required and there is limited space – please email Jackson.perry@ncparks.gov to register. This program is weather dependent.

item.description:
Join Ranger Gracie for a beginner-friendly bird walk to discover the birds of Pilot Mountain State Park during summer. We'll take a leisurely walk along park trails while learning how to spot and identify common birds by sight and sound. This program is perfect for first-time birders and for all ages. No experience or equipment needed, but if you have binoculars, bring them!
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Play Board Games at the Geekery — Thu Aug 20, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Triangle Board Games and Bars Come play games at Gamers Geekery and Tavern every thursday night!
Starting time is 6:30, but feel free to come in anytime and just hang out for the night. Group is very casual and friendly.
How it works: Come on in, grab a name tag and pay the $2.50 meetup participant fee at the bar area, find the tables that are reserved for the Meetup group, play games with others who show up. Food and drinks are available at the bar.
Please RSVP by noon day of. If less than four people are able to attend a given Wednesday the event will be canceled.
Source: Meetup: Triangle Board Games & Bars

Join the Media and Democracy Project to better understand and respond to the factors that influence public opinion, voters and democracy. Each session we will activate on a current information-related subject to help Fix Media Now.
We develop and distribute skills to navigate the Information War on truth and democracy.
We are a non-partisan all volunteer group that engages in actions to directly improve the quality of public information such as messaging, fighting disinformation, engaging in media accountability and in growing support for local journalism.

item.description:
RiverFest is Eden's signature annual festival celebrating the community's river heritage, outdoor recreation, arts, music, and small-town spirit. Held each September in Uptown Eden, the two-day event features live entertainment, local artisans, food vendors, family activities, historical exhibits, and river experiences. As part of America 250 NC, the festival will showcase the Dan River's connection to North Carolina's Revolutionary War history through special exhibits and educational programming, inviting visitors to experience the history, culture, and outdoor adventure that define Eden as North Carolina's Small Town, Big Outdoors destination.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Diplomacy Week 2026 — Mon Sep 28 — FedEx Global Education Center
item.description:
Join UNC Global Affairs for Diplomacy Week 2026 to celebrate 250 years of American diplomacy and the fifth anniversary of the Diplomacy Initiative. This weeklong series takes place Monday, Sept. 28, through Friday, Oct. 2, and will bring diplomats and public servants to Chapel Hill to celebrate the history of American diplomacy. Speakers bring experience and expertise in diplomacy, intelligence, the military and more.
UNC Global Affairs is pleased to partner with the Association of Diplomatic Studies and Training to host the traveling exhibition on the history of American diplomacy. The exhibition will be on display in the Florence and James Peacock Atrium in the FedEx Global Education Center from Monday to Friday.
Visit the Diplomacy Week 2026 webpage for a complete list of events.

item.title: Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage — Thu Oct 29, 10:00 AM — Gregg Museum of Art & Design
item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Fort Defiance House Tours — Thu Oct 29, 10:00 AM — Fort Defiance
item.description:
House tours are given on-demand Thursdays through Saturdays from 10 AM to 3 PM. Tours are also available on Sundays from 1:00 PM to 3:00 PM
Come learn about William Lenoir, a Captain during the American Revolution, who fought in the Battle of King's Mountain. You will also learn about his family, who inherited the house; the enslaved people who lived and worked on the plantation; and the site's history through the Civil War.
Tours last 45 minutes to an hour. Admission rates for tours are $7/adults and $5/children ages 14 and under
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: You Are Here Exhibition — Thu Oct 29, 10:00 AM — Witherspoon Student Center
item.description:
Join the African American Cultural Center to experience ariana Farquharson's You Are Here: Geolocating the Self through the Familiar in the Midst of the Unfamiliar. The exhibition is a speculative, immersive world-building study that invites guests to explore (geo)locating self and home amid a rapidly and frequently changing post-pandemic “new” world. It will be on display in the art gallery at the African American Cultural Center from Oct. 28, 2026, to Feb. 28, 2027. A behind-the-scenes look at the exhibition is set for Nov. 11.
Source: NC State African American Cultural Center
